claim: You can refresh the inventory of objects that an S3 File Gateway knows about using the console, the file system driven cache refresh process, or the RefreshCache API, and you get a CloudWatch Events notification when RefreshCache completes.

evidence.quote: Yes, you can refresh the inventory of objects that your Amazon S3 File Gateway knows about using the Console, the file system driven cache refresh process, or the RefreshCache API. claim: AWS recommends a single writer to the objects in an S3 bucket used with S3 File Gateway: if you directly overwrite or update an object that the gateway wrote, access through the file share has undefined behavior.

evidence.quote: We recommend a single writer to objects in your S3 bucket. If you directly overwrite or update an object previously written by File Gateway, it results in undefined behavior when the object is accessed through the file share.

claim: Several gateways can read from the same bucket: you can configure a file share as read-only and allow multiple gateways to read objects from the same bucket, refreshing the inventory with the console, the automated periodic cache refresh or the RefreshCache API.
question: Can several S3 File Gateways read the same bucket?

evidence.quote: Yes, you can have multiple readers on a bucket managed through an Amazon S3 File Gateway. You can configure a file share as read-only, and allow multiple gateways to read objects from the same bucket. Additionally, you can refresh the inventory of objects that your gateway knows about using the Storage Gateway Console, the automated periodic cache refresh process, or the RefreshCache API.

claim: AWS does not recommend several gateways writing to one bucket because it can lead to unpredictable results; you can enforce unique object names or prefixes, and S3 File Gateway emits health notifications when conflicts occur.
